description:
FILED s435 (Opus 5), found by THE FLIP and ruled a follow-up in the same
session (Fable, s435 review): the drop census has a SIXTH population it
cannot see, and nobody knew it was there.

tools/drop-census.pl, tools/corpus-diff.pl's SILENT-DROP counter and both
measurement runners' `drops` column all find drops by reading EMITTED .lisp
FILES.  A program run by fresh_perl_is / runperl is transpiled from a STRING
at run time (tools/pclperl-for-tests), so its emission is never a file in any
census population -- perl-tests (111), perl's t/ (527), lib/ (22),
cpan-tests modules (94), the board (28).  A drop in such a child is invisible
to every instrument the project has.

HOW IT SURFACED, which is the whole argument for fixing it: the flip made a
dropped statement DIE, and two rows that had been passing for years turned
out to be passing on nothing.

  perl-tests/split.t:682   fresh_perl_is(<<'CODE', '', {}, "scalar split stack overflow")
                           child: split//.0>60for"0000000000000000" ...
  perl-tests/bop.t:701     fresh_perl_is(<<'EOS', '', {}, "[perl #17844] access beyond end of block")
                           child: formline X000n^\\0,\\0^\\0for\0,0..10

Both assert the child prints NOTHING.  PCL dropped the child's only
statement, so the child printed nothing and the row passed -- while testing
nothing at all.  Post-flip the child dies and both rows fail honestly (they
are in docs/fail-baseline.tsv with that cause).  Attributed on a HEAD
worktree; each child probed alone against perl; bop.t's other two children
are unaffected.

So the s434 "five populations" completeness claim is true of FILES and false
of the whole compiled population.  The number of child-program drops is
UNKNOWN -- these two are simply the ones the flip happened to expose.

THE INSTRUMENT (ruled shape): tools/pclperl-for-tests records the drop
announcements from its child transpiles to a side channel -- a file named by
an env var the runner sets -- and the sweep aggregates a per-file
child-drops count beside the existing `drops` column.  Notes:
  - the child transpile already ANNOUNCES on stderr (task #339); what is
    missing is that the announcement goes to the CHILD's stderr, which the
    parent test captures as the child's OUTPUT and compares.  Do not route
    it there -- that is what makes a drop change a row's verdict.  A side
    channel keyed by env var is why this is a task and not a one-liner.
  - a child drop must NOT silently join the blessed census file: it is a
    different population with a different provenance.  Give it its own
    column or its own section, so a rise in one is never read as the other.
  - until this lands, docs/parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv's header says in
    so many words that child programs are not counted (edited s435).

ACCEPTANCE: a per-file child-drops count in the sweep's _status.tsv and in
the runner's report; the two known rows above appear in it; a file with no
fresh_perl child reports 0; the count does not change any row's verdict
(the side channel is not the child's stderr).  Then re-read the census
header note and replace "size unknown" with the measurement.


=== s438 (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE.  Pl::Parser::_announce_dropped_statement
gained one arm: when $PCL_DROP_LOG names a file, every drop appends
`FILE<TAB>LINE<TAB>TEXT<TAB>REASON` to it -- ungated by PCL_DROP_ANNOUNCE (it
must see module-mode drops, which announce nothing by ruling), never routed to
stderr (the child's stderr IS the row's observed output).  It records what the
census records, so: deduplicated per statement, a ruled Track-A refusal is not
logged (the file is refused, loudly, in every mode) and an eval-string drop is
not either (it DIES at transpile, #363, and emits nothing -- it is in no .lisp
population by construction).  The refusal predicate moved above the stderr gate
so the log arm can consult it; the DIE stayed below, so module mode is as
silent as it was.  No emission change: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files,
no generation bump.

sweep-perl-tests.pl sets it around the SBCL RUN only (never around the file's
own transpile, which would double-count the file's own drops), writes a
`child-drops` column into _status.tsv after `drops` (sweep-diff reads the first
six columns and ignores it -- REPORTED, NOT GATED, per the s437 ruling) and
prints TWO numbers, because either alone lies: the per-file COUNT (what that
file's run lost; it double-counts the harness, which every file re-transpiles
under *pcl-skip-cache*) and the DISTINCT SITES across the corpus with how many
files reached each (the census view).

FIRST MEASUREMENT (full sweep, 108 files): 241 drops in 98 files, TEN distinct
sites.
  * perl-tests/t/test.pl:179 and :180, in 98 of 98 files -- `open(my $f, '<',
    $out) ? <$f> // '' : ''` in runperl_and_capture.  Filed #479, which also
    records that the line is WRONG IN REAL PERL (`my $f` in a ternary's
    condition is not in scope in its branches; the function returns ('','')
    for a file with content).  closure.t alone contributes 38 of the 241 by
    loading test.pl nineteen times.
  * SIX one-off fresh_perl/runperl child programs, which is the whole child
    population: bop.t's formline and split.t's split (this task's two known
    cases -- both reproduced), blocks.t x2 `BEGIN(){...}`, lex.t's
    `sub ub(){0} ub ub` (runperl) and `flock _$`, magic.t's bare `]`.  Four of
    the six are programs perl itself rejects.
  * ONE run-time MODULE load, and a real gap in a real module: the system
    perl's Devel/Peek.pm:59 `$num |= (1<<index($D_flags,$_)) for split //,
    $on;` -- PPI lexes `<<index` as a HEREDOC.  Filed #483.
A file with no fresh_perl child reports 0 (10 of the 108 did).  No row's
verdict moved: sweep GATE clean, TOTAL 18312 (+0), 0 new / 0 fixed.

The census header's "size unknown" paragraph is replaced by that measurement.
Rule written into docs/test-infrastructure.md.  NOT DONE, deliberately: the
companion runner (tools/run-perl-suite.pl) does not set PCL_DROP_LOG -- the
ruling named the sweep, and the second consumer should measure first the same
way.
subject: The drop census has a SIXTH, UNCOUNTED population: fresh_perl/runperl CHILD programs (transpiled from a string at run time, so they are in no .lisp population) -- two known, both were ACCIDENTAL PASSES the s435 flip exposed
